mainTopic: Animals blemished before their הקדש: redeeming their babies, slaughtering them outside, תמורה, and redemption after death
overview: This amud continues the discussion of animals that already had a lasting מום before they were made holy. Such animals have only קדושת דמים. First the גמרא proves from a ברייתא that their babies can be redeemed without a מום, because the טפל cannot be stricter than the עיקר. From that reason it learns that a healthy male dedicated 'for its value' gets קדושת הגוף, which supports רבא. Next it turns to the משנה's ruling that slaughtering these animals outside is פטור. רבי אלעזר reads 'חייב' and places the case at a private במה. His source is an extra פסוק, 'לא תזבח', and the גמרא tests that source against בכור, מעשר, תמורה and ולדות, showing that each already has its own source. Then it explains why such an animal cannot make a תמורה, learning this from the extra words 'טוב ברע'. Finally, רב says that 'if they died, they are redeemed' follows רבי שמעון. The opposing חכמים are identified with the school of לוי, but the word 'אוֹתָהּ' is a problem for that view. The גמרא then begins a challenge to רב that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can the babies of value-holy animals be redeemed while unblemished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the babies of animals with only קדושת דמים can be redeemed without a מום, or whether they must wait until they get one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they redeemed while unblemished, or are they not redeemed while unblemished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the babies of animals that were holy only for their value: can you redeem them right away while they are still healthy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby of an animal with full קדושת הגוף is born holy and cannot be redeemed until it gets a מום. The mother here had only קדושת דמים, so the question is whether the baby follows her lighter holiness or gets full holiness of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: They are redeemed (bought out of their holiness with money)
Unblemished, healthy animals
Holiness of value only. The animal itself is not offered; its money belongs to הקדש
The offspring, the baby of the animal

phrases.english: Are they redeemed while unblemished,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the babies of animals that were holy only for their money value, because they already had a lasting blemish when they were dedicated.

phrases.english: or are they not redeemed while unblemished?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים אוֹ אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that follows from the משנה's discussion of animals whose מום came before their הקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the offspring of קדושת דמים animals may be redeemed while unblemished, or must wait for a מום.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the babies may be sold without a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if someone dedicates permanently blemished animals for the altar and they give birth, the babies may be sold without a מום, so the secondary holiness is not stricter than the main holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who dedicates animals with permanent blemishes for the altar, and they gave birth, the babies are sold and do not need a blemish. This is because holiness does not take hold of them, so that the secondary should not be stricter than the main.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא: the babies of permanently blemished dedicated animals can be sold right away, without a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother could never go on the altar, so her holiness is only קדושת דמים and she can be redeemed at once. The baby's holiness comes from the mother (טפל), so it cannot be stronger than hers (עיקר). That proves the babies may be redeemed while unblemished.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. The usual way the גמרא brings a source as a proof
One who dedicates (makes something holy)
Permanent blemishes
They may be sold, meaning redeemed
Secondary; something that comes from the main thing
The main thing; here, the mother

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that the holiness of a baby animal can never be stronger than the holiness of its mother.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who dedicates animals with permanent blemishes
for the altar, and they gave birth,
they are sold, and they do not need a blemish,
because holiness does not take hold of them,
phrases.notes: He means altar-level holiness. The babies don't become holy enough to be offered.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר.
phrases.english: so that the secondary should not be stricter than the main.
phrases.notes: The baby is the secondary and the mother is the main. The baby's holiness can't be stronger than hers.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That babies of קדושת דמים animals may be redeemed without a מום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about babies of permanently blemished animals dedicated for the altar.

steps.title: Learning from the ברייתא's reason: a healthy male gets full holiness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא focuses on the reason the ברייתא gives. Holiness fails only because the baby cannot be stricter than the mother. So someone who dedicates a healthy male 'for its value' gives it קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is only so that the secondary should not be stricter than the main. But if one dedicated a male animal for its value, it becomes holy with holiness of its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a side lesson from the ברייתא's exact reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only reason the babies lack altar holiness is that they come from a blemished mother, then holiness itself was not the problem. So when a healthy male is dedicated directly, even if the person said 'for its value', full קדושת הגוף takes hold, because the animal could go on the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is. The גמרא is pointing out that this is the only reason
For its value (money)
Holiness of the body itself. The animal itself must be offered

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that saying 'for its value' always makes only קדושת דמים. With a healthy male that could go on the altar, it becomes holy in its body anyway.

phrases.english: The reason is so that the secondary should not be
stricter than the main,
but if one dedicated a male for its value,
it is holy with holiness of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר, אֲבָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes a new inference from the reasoning of the ברייתא brought in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Dedicating a healthy male for its value gives it קדושת הגוף.

steps.title: This supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this inference supports רבא, who said the same thing: a male dedicated for its value gets קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבא, because רבא said: if one dedicated a male for its value, it is holy with holiness of its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the lesson it just learned from the ברייתא backs up a statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling is the same as the inference from step 3. The ברייתא therefore gives רבא's view support from an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: This supports him
רבא, a leading אמורא of בבל

steps.whatToRemember: The babies of קדושת דמים animals can be redeemed without a מום, because the טפל is not stricter than the עיקר. A healthy male dedicated 'for its value' gets קדושת הגוף, like רבא.

phrases.english: This supports רבא,
for רבא said:
If one dedicated a male for its value,
it is holy with holiness of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the inference of step 3 to רבא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a male dedicated for its value has קדושת הגוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the ברייתא's reason in step 3.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: slaughtering them outside is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: someone who slaughters these animals, whose מום came before their הקדש, outside the עזרה is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its ruling about slaughtering these animals outside. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals could never be offered, so killing them outside is not the sin of שחוטי חוץ. The quote prepares for רבי אלעזר's different reading.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters them outside the עזרה
Exempt; not punished

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means animals that had a lasting blemish before they were made holy, the case of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the babies and returns to quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering animals whose מום preceded their הקדש outside the עזרה is פטור.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's reading: liable, about a private altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads the משנה as 'חייב' and explains it as talking about a private altar (במת יחיד).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר teaches it as 'liable', and he explains it as being about a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר has a different version of the משנה's word: 'liable' instead of 'exempt'. He explains it as a case of a במת יחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read as 'liable', the משנה would clash with the rule that a blemished animal cannot be a שחוטי חוץ. So רבי אלעזר places it at a private במה: there the person is liable for offering a blemished animal, not for slaughtering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches (reads the text as)
Liable, deserving punishment
He sets it up as (explains the case as)
A private altar of one person, allowed at certain times in history

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר teaches it as 'liable,'
and he explains it as being about a private altar.
phrases.notes: So he is liable for offering a blemished animal on his own altar, not for slaughtering outside the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַתְנֵי חַיָּיב, וּמוֹקֵי לַהּ בְּבָמַת יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the משנה line quoted in step 5, with an explanation of the case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אלעזר's version the משנה says 'חייב', and it refers to offering on a במת יחיד.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: a blemished animal on a private altar is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר derives from 'לא תזבח לה׳ אלקיך שור ושה' that a person who sacrifices a blemished animal on a בָּמַת יָחִיד, at a time when private altars are allowed, violates a לאו. The main altar is already covered by 'עורת או שבור', so this פסוק must be about the private altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר said: How do we know that someone who sacrifices a blemished animal on a private altar, at a time when private altars are allowed, breaks a לאו? The פסוק says, 'Do not sacrifice to ה׳ your God an ox or a sheep that has a blemish.' This cannot be needed for the big public altar, because another פסוק already covers that ('blind or broken...'). So apply it to a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי אלעזר's reading of the משנה from Step 6 by quoting his own teaching. That teaching shows there is a real prohibition against offering blemished animals on a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים forbid blemished sacrifices. The one in ויקרא already covers the main altar, so the one in דברים would be extra. An extra פסוק is never wasted, so רבי אלעזר uses it for the private altar. That is why the slaughterer in the משנה can be 'חייב'.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar that an individual may build, used in periods when this was allowed
The time periods when private altars were permitted
The great public altar, like the one in the משכן
A negative commandment, a 'do not' prohibition

keyTerms.term: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְ... תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְ...
keyTerms.meaning: If a פסוק is not needed for its plain topic, apply it to a different topic

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two altars. The פסוק 'עורת או שבור' is about the main altar. The פסוק 'לא תזבח' is being moved over to the private altar only because the main altar is already covered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי אלעזר can read the משנה as 'חייב': the slaughter on a private altar breaks a real לאו.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know that one who slaughters a blemished animal
on a private altar
at a time when private altars are permitted,
that he violates a prohibition?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא תִזְבַּח לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה״,
phrases.english: As it is said: "You shall not sacrifice to ה׳ your God an ox or a sheep"
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues 'that has a blemish in it.' That is the part being used here.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the great altar,
since it is written: "Blind or broken, etc."
phrases.notes: This is a פסוק in ויקרא that already forbids blemished animals on the main altar.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִנַּיִן לַזּוֹבֵחַ בְּהֵמָה בַּעֲלַת מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for רבי אלעזר's explanation of 'חייב' in Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sacrificing a blemished animal on a בָּמַת יָחִיד during היתר הבמות is a לאו, learned from the extra פסוק 'לא תזבח'.

steps.title: Why not apply the extra verse to a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: maybe the extra פסוק should be applied to a בכור. A בכור becomes holy even when it is born blemished, so one might think it can also be offered while blemished. The פסוק would then teach that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: if the פסוק is not needed for regular sacrifices, apply it to a firstborn. You might have thought that since a firstborn becomes holy even when blemished, it can also be offered when blemished. The פסוק teaches that it cannot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's choice of what the extra פסוק teaches. It suggests a different use for it: the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'extra פסוק' method only tells us the פסוק must teach something new. It does not tell us what. A blemished בכור is a real new case, because its holiness takes hold even with a מום. So the פסוק might be teaching about the בכור and not about the private altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular sacrificial animals
A firstborn kosher animal, which is holy from birth
It might enter your mind to say (what you would have thought)
It teaches us

phrases.english: Say instead: if it is not needed for regular sacrifices
apply it to the matter of a firstborn,
for it might enter your mind to say:
since it becomes holy even when it is blemished,
let it also be offered when it is blemished,
so the verse teaches us that it is not so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְקָדָשִׁים תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לִבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how Step 7 applies the extra פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's use of the extra פסוק for a בָּמַת יָחִיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra פסוק could just as well teach that a blemished בכור, though holy, may not be offered.

steps.title: The firstborn already has its own explicit verse
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the law of a blemished בכור is written openly in its own פסוק, 'פסח או עור לא תזבחנו'. So the extra פסוק is not needed for בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: about a firstborn it is written openly, 'lame or blind... you shall not sacrifice it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The בכור cannot be what the extra פסוק teaches, because the בכור already has its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is 'extra' can only be used for a case that is not already covered. The בכור's ban on blemished offerings appears openly in דברים פרק ט״ו. So the בכור option fails, and רבי אלעזר's private-altar reading stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: They said (an answer given by the Sages)
Explicitly, openly

phrases.english: They answered:
about a firstborn it is written explicitly
"lame or blind... you shall not sacrifice it."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in the section about the בכור in דברים פרק ט״ו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the alternative case is already covered by its own פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra פסוק might teach about a blemished בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בכור has its own explicit פסוק, so the extra פסוק is free to teach about the private altar.

steps.title: Why not apply the extra verse to the animal tithe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe the extra פסוק should be applied to מעשר בהמה. A tithed animal becomes holy even with a מום, since 'לא יבקר בין טוב לרע'. So one might think it can be offered with its מום, and the פסוק would teach that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: if the פסוק is not needed for regular sacrifices, apply it to the animal tithe. You might have thought that since it becomes holy even with its blemish, as it is written, 'He shall not check whether it is good or bad,' it can also be offered with its blemish. The פסוק teaches that it cannot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same challenge again, this time with מעשר בהמה in place of בכור. Step 11 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a בכור, a tithed animal becomes holy even when blemished, because the owner may not pick and choose good from bad. That makes it another real candidate for the extra פסוק. Unlike בכור, the גמרא has not yet shown that מעשר has its own explicit פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal is made holy
He shall not check whether it is good or bad. The tenth animal is holy no matter what
With its blemish

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step ends the discussion. Step 11 answers this challenge.

phrases.english: But say: if it is not needed for regular sacrifices
apply it to the matter of the animal tithe,
for it might enter your mind to say:
since it becomes holy with its blemish,
as it is written: "He shall not check whether it is good or bad,"
let it also be offered with its blemish,
so the verse teaches us that it is not so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְקָדָשִׁים תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of Step 8, now using מעשר instead of בכור
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's use of the extra פסוק for a בָּמַת יָחִיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tithed animal also becomes holy while blemished, so the extra פסוק could teach that it may not be offered.

steps.title: The tithe is learned from the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the מעשר בהמה challenge. מעשר does not need the extra פסוק, because a גזירה שוה of ׳העברה׳ links it to בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: מעשר also learns from בכור through the shared word ׳passing׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. The law of a blemished מעשר בהמה already comes from בכור, so the extra פסוק is not needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ׳העברה׳ (passing) appears by בכור and also by מעשר. This shared word is a גזירה שוה, and it carries the rule of בכור over to מעשר. Since a blemished בכור cannot be offered (Step 9), a blemished מעשר cannot be offered either, so the extra פסוק is still free for רבי אלעזר's בָּמַת יָחִיד.

keyTerms.meaning: They say. The usual way the גמרא opens an answer.
Here it means מעשר בהמה, every tenth animal of the herd.
Learns, derives one law from another.
Passing. The shared word that makes the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: They say: the tithe also
learns ׳passing׳ ׳passing׳ from the firstborn.
phrases.notes: The firstborn are ׳passed׳ to ה׳, and tithed animals ׳pass under the rod׳. The same word links the two laws.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי גָּמַר הַעֲבָרָה הַעֲבָרָה מִבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מעשר challenge raised in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a different source (a גזירה שוה from בכור) already covers the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra פסוק is needed to teach that a blemished מעשר cannot be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר learns from בכור by ׳העברה׳, so the extra פסוק stays free for בָּמַת יָחִיד.

steps.title: Maybe the verse is about a substitute animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the extra פסוק might teach about תמורה. A substitute becomes holy even when it is blemished, so one might think it can be offered blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that the פסוק is about תמורה. You might think that since a substitute becomes holy even with a מום, it can also be offered with its מום. The פסוק would teach that it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third possible use for the extra פסוק: תמורה, an animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a substitute becomes holy even if it is ׳bad for good׳, meaning even if it is blemished. That could lead someone to think a blemished תמורה may go on the altar. If so, the extra פסוק would be needed to teach that it may not, and it would no longer be free for רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply it to the matter of. Use a spare פסוק for a different case.
A substitute. An animal someone tries to swap for a קרבן. It becomes holy too.
It would enter your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken thought.
It teaches us.

phrases.english: Say: apply it to the matter
of a substitute for sacrificial animals,
for it would enter your mind to say:
since it becomes holy when it is blemished,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: as it is written: ׳He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, etc.׳
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says ׳a good for a bad, or a bad for a good׳, and that both become holy. That is why even a blemished substitute is holy.

phrases.english: it may also be offered when it is blemished,
it teaches us that it may not!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לִתְמוּרַת קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מעשר is handled, the גמרא tries another case that could use up the extra פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim in Step 7 that the extra פסוק must be about בָּמַת יָחִיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תמורה becomes holy even when blemished, so a פסוק is needed to stop it from being offered. That job would use up the extra פסוק.

steps.title: A substitute is compared to the original animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ׳והיה הוא ותמורתו׳ compares the תמורה to the original קרבן. A blemished original cannot be offered, so a blemished תמורה cannot be offered either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ׳it and its substitute׳. This compares the substitute to the original. Just as the original cannot be offered with a מום, so too its substitute cannot be offered with a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the תמורה challenge. A different פסוק already teaches that a blemished תמורה cannot be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the Torah puts ׳it׳ and ׳its substitute׳ side by side, it makes a היקש: the substitute follows the rules of the original. The original cannot be offered if blemished, so neither can the substitute. The extra פסוק is again left free for בָּמַת יָחִיד.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says.
Compares. This is a היקש, where the Torah links two things so they share the same laws.
It and its substitute.

phrases.english: The verse states: ׳Then it and its substitute shall be holy׳,
it compares its substitute to it:
just as it, when blemished, is not offered,
so too its substitute, when blemished, is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תמורה challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a היקש in a different פסוק already covers the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra פסוק is needed to stop a blemished תמורה from being offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: ׳הוא ותמורתו׳ compares the substitute to the original, so the extra פסוק stays free.

steps.title: רבי זירא: maybe the verse is about offspring of sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests the extra פסוק might teach about ולדות קדשים. Offspring are holy even when blemished because of their mother, so one might think they can be offered blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenges: say the פסוק is about the offspring of קדשים. You might think that since they are holy even with a מום because of their mother, they can also be offered with a מום. The פסוק would teach that they cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא raises a new challenge to רבי אלעזר. Maybe the extra פסוק is about the babies born to animals that were already קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offspring's holiness comes from its mother, not from anyone dedicating it. So it is holy even if it is born blemished. That could suggest it may be offered blemished, and the extra פסוק would be needed to say no. That would take the פסוק away from בָּמַת יָחִיד. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it. This introduces a sharp challenge.
An אמורא who raises this challenge.
Offspring of קדשים. Babies born to animals that were already dedicated.
On account of their mother. Their holiness comes from her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to it:
say, apply it to the matter of offspring of sacrificial animals,
for it would enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּקְדוֹשִׁין כְּשֶׁהֵן בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אַגַּב אִמָּן,
phrases.english: since they are holy when they are blemished, on account of their mother,
they may also be offered when they are blemished,
it teaches us that they may not!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֵימָא, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְוַלְדוֹת קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After תמורה is handled, רבי זירא proposes yet another case that could use up the extra פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim in Step 7 that the extra פסוק must be about בָּמַת יָחִיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Offspring of קדשים are holy even when blemished, so a פסוק is needed to stop them from being offered. That job would use up the extra פסוק.

steps.title: רבא: Offspring Are Already Covered by a הקש to a נדר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רבי זירא. The school of רבי ישמעאל already learned that blemished ולדות (and תמורות) cannot be offered, by comparing them to a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the school of רבי ישמעאל already settled this. They taught: 'Only your holy things which you have, and your vows.' 'Your holy things' means substitutes. 'Which you have' means offspring. 'And your vows' means the פסוק compares them to a vow. A blemished vowed animal can't be offered, so these can't be offered blemished either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from step 14. The extra פסוק isn't needed to teach about ולדות, because a different פסוק already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא wanted to use the extra פסוק to teach that blemished ולדות can't be offered. רבא points to a הקש in דברים י״ב, which puts תמורות and ולדות next to נדרים. Since a blemished נדר can never be offered, neither can they. So the extra פסוק is still free for its other use.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
A comparison the Torah makes by placing two things together in one פסוק
A vow, here an animal someone pledged as a קרבן
Offspring of holy animals
Settled it, ruled on it

steps.whatToRemember: Blemished ולדות and תמורות are both disqualified through the הקש to נדר, so the extra פסוק does not have to teach this.

phrases.english: Rava says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael already settled it,
phrases.notes: He means this question about blemished offspring was already answered from a different פסוק.

phrases.english: as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Only your holy things which you have, and your vows"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in דברים י״ב:כ״ו.

phrases.english: "Only your holy things": these are the substitutes,
"which you have": these are the offspring,
"and your vows": the verse compared them to a vow,
just as a vowed animal with a blemish may not be offered,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָנֵי נָמֵי בַּעַל מוּם לֹא.
phrases.english: so too these, with a blemish, may not be offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's suggestion that the extra פסוק teaches about ולדות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate source already covers the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra פסוק is needed to stop blemished ולדות from being offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: A הקש to נדר already teaches this, so the extra פסוק is not needed for ולדות.

steps.title: Why Can't It Make a Substitute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that an animal blemished before its הקדש does not make a תמורה, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said such animals do not make a substitute holy. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is discussing an animal that had a מום before it was made holy. Normally, if someone tries to swap a holy animal for another one, the new animal becomes holy too. Here the משנה says that does not happen, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal, which becomes holy too
What is the reason?

phrases.english: "And they do not make a substitute"
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the extra-פסוק discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that an animal blemished before הקדש does not create a תמורה.

steps.title: An Extra Phrase Teaches: Only an Animal Good From the Start Makes a Substitute
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר'. One half of 'good for bad, bad for good' seems extra, so it teaches that only an animal that was טוב מעיקרו can make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good.' Now, if you already said a bad for a good is forbidden, do you need to say a good for a bad? So the extra words teach this: an animal that was good from the start makes a substitute. An animal that was bad from the start does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading a lesson into words of the פסוק that seem extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists both directions of a swap. The גמרא argues that once one direction is forbidden, the other is obvious, so the second mention must be teaching something new. That new lesson is that only an animal that was unblemished (טוב) when it became holy can create a תמורה. One that was blemished from the start (רע מעיקרו) cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not exchange it nor substitute it (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳)
Now, if already…: introduces a 'this is obvious' argument
Is it needed to say?
From the start, meaning at the time it was made holy

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that was blemished before it was made holy cannot make a תמורה. This is learned from the extra wording 'טוב ברע ורע בטוב'.

phrases.english: For the verse says:
"He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, etc."
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the פסוק: 'a good for a bad, or a bad for a good.'

phrases.english: Now, if you said a bad for a good is forbidden,
is it necessary to say a good for a bad?
Rather, one that was good from the start makes a substitute,
one that was bad from the start does not make a substitute.
phrases.notes: 'Bad from the start' means it already had a blemish when it was made holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seemingly extra phrase in ויקרא כ״ז:י׳ teaches that only an animal unblemished at its הקדש makes a תמורה.

steps.title: 'If They Died, They Are Redeemed' Follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's ruling that such animals can be redeemed even after death matches רבי שמעון. He holds that only קדשי מזבח needed העמדה והערכה, while קדשי בדק הבית did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if they died, they are redeemed. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this is the view of רבי שמעון. He said that animals holy for the altar were included in the rule of standing and valuation, but things holy for Temple upkeep were not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, and רב identifies which תנא it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem certain holy animals, they must be stood before a כהן and valued (העמדה והערכה). A dead animal can't be stood up, so it can't be redeemed. רבי שמעון says only altar-holy animals need this. So an animal that doesn't need it can be redeemed even after it dies.

keyTerms.meaning: They are redeemed, meaning exchanged for money and made non-holy
Things made holy to be offered on the altar
Things made holy for Temple upkeep, holy only for their money value
Standing the animal before a כהן and having him set its value

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה's animal was made holy for the altar, yet it can be redeemed after death. The next step explains this: רבי שמעון treats an animal blemished from the start like בדק הבית, because it doesn't need העמדה והערכה.

phrases.english: "If they died, they are redeemed."
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
This is the view of Rabbi Shimon, who said:

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: things holy for the altar were included in standing and valuation,

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.
phrases.english: things holy for Temple upkeep were not included in standing and valuation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and identifies its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redeeming such animals after death follows רבי שמעון, who limits העמדה והערכה to קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: The משנה Showing רבי שמעון's View
steps.stepSummary: A משנה is quoted in which רבי שמעון says בדק הבית animals that die can be redeemed. He agrees that an animal blemished from the start can also be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון says, things holy for Temple upkeep, if they died, are redeemed. And רבי שמעון agrees about an animal blemished from the start that it is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה (in תמורה) as the source for רב's claim about רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line shows רבי שמעון's basic rule for בדק הבית. The second line connects it to our משנה. Even an altar animal that had a מום before its הקדש is treated as not needing העמדה והערכה, so it too can be redeemed after death.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
And he agrees
An animal that had a blemish before it was made holy

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, אִם מֵתוּ — יִפָּדוּ.
phrases.english: things holy for Temple upkeep, if they died, are redeemed.
And Rabbi Shimon agrees
regarding one blemished from the start, that it is redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source supporting רב's statement in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה's 'if they died, they are redeemed' matches רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תמורה where רבי שמעון rules this way about בדק הבית and about an animal blemished from the start.

steps.title: The Word 'אוֹתָהּ' Excludes an Animal Blemished From the Start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון agrees about an animal blemished from the start. It answers that the word 'אותה' in the valuation פסוקים leaves it out of העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says 'it'. The word 'it' comes to exclude an animal that was blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי שמעון's agreement and answers it right away with a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about standing and valuing an animal (ויקרא כ״ז:י״א-י״ב) say 'it'. The גמרא reads this as limiting the rule to an animal that was fit when it was made holy. An animal blemished from the start is left out of העמדה והערכה, so it can be redeemed even after death.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It', a limiting word in the פסוק
To exclude

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, an animal that had a מום before its הקדש does not need העמדה והערכה. So it can be redeemed even after it dies, which explains our משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says: "it"
phrases.notes: This is from ויקרא כ״ז, about standing the animal before the כהן and valuing 'it'.

phrases.english: "it": to exclude one blemished from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's agreement quoted in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limiting word 'אותה' excludes an animal blemished before הקדש from העמדה והערכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה's 'if they died, they are redeemed' follows רבי שמעון, based on the word 'אותה'.

steps.title: The חכמים say dead animals are buried, but who are they?
steps.stepSummary: The quote from the משנה in תמורה ends with the חכמים, who say dead consecrated animals must be buried. The גמרא asks which תנא they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים say: if they died, they must be buried. Who are these חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from step 19, where the חכמים disagree with רבי שמעון. Then it asks which תנא the חכמים are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that בדק הבית animals that die can be redeemed. The חכמים say that any consecrated animal that dies must be buried, because it can no longer be stood up and valued. The גמרא wants to know which known opinion stands behind this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the group that disagrees with רבי שמעון here
They must be buried, so no one may benefit from them
Who? (Aramaic)

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
If they died, they must be buried.
Who are the Sages?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 19 and asks who the opposing חכמים are.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is behind the חכמים's ruling that dead consecrated animals are buried.

steps.title: The חכמים are the school of לוי, who include every animal
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are the תנא דבי לוי, who taught that every animal, even one blemished from the start, was included in העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the תנא of the school of לוי, as the school of לוי taught: Everything was included in standing and valuation, even an animal blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים follow the teaching of the school of לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every consecrated animal needs העמדה והערכה, then a dead animal can never be redeemed, because a dead animal cannot be stood up. This explains why the חכמים say all dead animals are buried. It also means they do not agree with the exception for an animal blemished from the start, which רבי שמעון accepted in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the school of לוי, a collection of ברייתות
Standing the animal before the כהן so he can value it
An animal that was blemished even before it was consecrated

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups. רבי שמעון agreed that a blemished-from-the-start animal is left out of העמדה והערכה. The school of לוי says even that animal is included.

phrases.english: It is the tanna of the school of Levi,
as the school of Levi taught:
All were included in standing and valuation,
even an animal blemished from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי הוּא, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are the תנא דבי לוי, who hold that every animal, even one blemished from the start, needs העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: Levi's own collection includes even a חיה and an עוף
steps.stepSummary: In Levi's own collection of ברייתות, the school of לוי goes further: even a wild animal and a bird need העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the school of לוי taught in its own collection: even a wild animal, even a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how far the school of לוי takes its rule. Even animals that can never go on the מזבח are included in העמדה והערכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חיה and an עוף can never be brought as a קרבן, yet Levi still includes them. This shows that for him, 'everything' really means everything, with no exceptions at all.

keyTerms.meaning: His own collection of ברייתות (here, Levi's)
A wild, non-domesticated animal
A bird

phrases.english: And similarly the school of Levi taught in his collection:
Even a wild animal, even a bird,
phrases.notes: He means these too were included in standing and valuation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי בְּמַתְנִיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 22 by showing that Levi's rule has no exceptions.
steps.raayaObject: That the school of לוי includes absolutely every animal in העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: The word 'אוֹתָהּ' should leave something out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Levi: the פסוק says 'אוֹתָהּ', which should exclude at least something.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'אוֹתָהּ'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the school of לוי from the word 'אוֹתָהּ' in the valuation פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 we saw that 'אוֹתָהּ' is read as a limiting word that leaves some animal out of העמדה והערכה. If Levi includes everything, even a חיה and an עוף, then 'אוֹתָהּ' leaves nothing out, and the word seems to teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? It opens a challenge from a פסוק
'It,' a word read as limiting the rule

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "it"!
phrases.notes: This is the word from the valuation פסוקים, 'and the כהן shall value it,' that we met in step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב ״אוֹתָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the view in steps 22 and 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The school of לוי's claim that every animal needs העמדה והערכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אוֹתָהּ' is a limiting word, so it must exclude something. A view that excludes nothing ignores it.

steps.title: The גמרא admits 'אוֹתָהּ' is a problem for Levi
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that the word 'אוֹתָהּ' is a real difficulty for the school of לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'אוֹתָהּ' is a difficulty for the תנא of the school of לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives no answer. It admits that the question stands against the school of לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קַשְׁיָא' here means the challenge is left without a solution. The school of לוי's view is weakened, but the גמרא does not throw it out entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים who say dead animals are buried follow the school of לוי, who includes every animal in העמדה והערכה. The word 'אוֹתָהּ' remains an unanswered problem for that view.

phrases.english: "It" is difficult for the tanna of the school of Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אוֹתָהּ״ לְתָנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits that the challenge of step 24 has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The school of לוי's view stands against the word 'אוֹתָהּ' with no answer.

steps.title: Do the regular רבנן also redeem a blemished animal after death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון. Perhaps they also read 'אוֹתָהּ' as excluding the blemished-from-the-start animal, so it could be redeemed after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון, what do they hold? Do they really agree that if such animals died, they can be redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון. It asks whether they too accept the 'אוֹתָהּ' exclusion and would allow redemption after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'אוֹתָהּ' must exclude something, the רבנן may well agree that an animal blemished from the start is left out of העמדה והערכה. If so, they would also let it be redeemed after death. This would mean the משנה in בכורות is not only רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with him
Is it indeed so? It checks whether a conclusion really follows
They can be redeemed

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי?
phrases.english: But the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon, what?
Is it indeed so that if they died they may be redeemed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the strength of the 'אוֹתָהּ' reading to ask about the regular רבנן's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון also hold that a blemished-from-the-start animal can be redeemed after death.

steps.title: If so, the גמרא starts to challenge רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge: if the רבנן also agree, why did רב say the משנה matches only רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a challenge against רב that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the רבנן allow redemption after death for a blemished-from-the-start animal, then the משנה fits everyone. That would make רב's statement in step 18, that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; it opens a challenge built on what was just said

phrases.english: If so,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of step 26 into a challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement in step 18 that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן agree too, the משנה is everyone's view, so tying it to רבי שמעון makes no sense.
